is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles funestus, Anopheles gambiae, and Anopheles ziemanni (Abstract, Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes L1014F, N1575Y, G119S-Ace1, L119F-GSTe2, CYP6P9a, and CYP6P9b (Table 1, Table 4).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 4 provides genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) for all markers across the studied species.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Penka-Michel, Western Highlands of Cameroon, using human landing catches (Methods, Page 2-3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting original entomological and molecular data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for Penka-Michel, specifically the sites Bazinza and Quartier lac (Methods, Page 3; Fig 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted over a 12-month period from September 2023 to August 2024 (Abstract, Page 1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study is part of the ReMA project, but presents a specific longitudinal dataset for Penka-Michel (Ethics, Page 15).

supplement.evidence: The primary genotype data required is provided in Table 4 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This longitudinal study (2023-2024) in Penka-Michel, Cameroon, characterizes malaria transmission and insecticide resistance in An. funestus, An. gambiae, and An. ziemanni. It reports high frequencies of target-site (L1014F, N1575Y, G119S-Ace1) and metabolic (L119F-GSTe2, CYP6P9a/b) resistance markers, with genotype counts provided for each.
